questions.q:

Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.

[CGL PRE 2024]
questions.s:
The correct answer is: he is as smarter as


"as smarter as" is incorrect because we don't use the comparative form (smarter) with "as...as." Instead, we use the positive degree of the adjective, which is "smart." So, the correct form is "as smart as".

questions.q: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
o: so better as
in this country is
No other place
questions.s:
CorrectAnswer: so better as
Explanation: The phrase "so better as" is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "so much better as" or simply "better than," as comparisons involving adjectives like "better" do not require "so better as.

questions.q:
From the given options, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Earnest wrote (A)/the most perfect (B)/correspondence today. (C)/No error (D)
questions.s:
The error lies in part 'B'.
Key Points

  • The given above sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
  • Here, 'a perfect' will be used instead of 'the most perfect'.
  • As a general rule, some adjectives like unique, ideal, perfect, extreme, complete, universal, infinite, perpetual, entire, whole, round, chief, etc. are not compared i.e. they are not used in comparative or superlative degrees.
  • We can not use superlative or comparative degree (more/most) before these adjectives.
  • Example:
    • It is a unique book. 
    • It is the most unique book. 
  • ​​Therefore, as per the given points, the most appropriate option is Option 1.
     

Correct sentence: Earnest wrote a perfect correspondence today.

The more loud they would scream
questions.s: For parallel comparison in "the more... the more...", 'loud' should be in its comparative form 'louder'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Aren’t you such young to travel by yourself?
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'such young'. 

Key Points

  • The erroneous Part 'such young' should be 'so young'. 
  • We know that 'Such' is a determiner. Whereas, 'So' is an adverb. 
  • They often have the same meaning of ''very'' or ''to this degree''.
  • We use such+noun phrases. And so+adjective or adverb phrase. 
    • Example: 
      • She is such a great cook.
      • Those chocolates are so good.
  • Here, in the given question 'Young' is used as an adjective.
  • Therefore, 'So' will be used. 
    ​

The correct sentence is: Aren't you so young to travel by yourself?
